title: Cardiac emergencies and arrhythmias
summary: Manage the cardiac emergencies an ICU sees every day: STEMI and NSTE-ACS reperfusion and antithrombotics, acute heart failure and pulmonary oedema, AF with rapid ventricular response, ventricular and wide-complex tachycardia, bradycardia and temporary pacing, and hypertensive emergencies with target-driven BP lowering.

topics.title: Acute coronary syndromes: STEMI and NSTE-ACS
topics.summary: ECG within 10 min. STEMI: primary PCI if achievable within 120 min of diagnosis, otherwise fibrinolysis within 10 min and transfer. Load antiplatelets, anticoagulate, and risk-stratify NSTE-ACS for timing of angiography.

steps.title: 12-lead ECG
steps.detail: STEMI: new ST elevation ≥ 1 mm in 2 contiguous leads (V2-V3 ≥ 2.5 mm men < 40 y, ≥ 2 mm men ≥ 40 y, ≥ 1.5 mm women), LBBB/paced rhythm with ischaemic symptoms, posterior MI (ST depression V1-V3). Repeat every 15-30 min if non-diagnostic.

steps.title: Initial care
steps.detail: Monitor, IV access, O2 only if SpO2 < 90%, aspirin 150-300 mg, cautious IV opioid, GTN if no hypotension or RV infarct. High-sensitivity troponin 0/1 h or 0/2 h.

steps.title: Reperfusion decision
steps.detail: Symptoms < 12 h: primary PCI if diagnosis-to-wire ≤ 120 min; otherwise fibrinolysis within 10 min of diagnosis.

steps.title: Give
steps.detail: Tenecteplase by weight (half dose if ≥ 75 y) + clopidogrel 300 mg (75 mg if > 75 y) + enoxaparin or UFH.

steps.title: After lysis
steps.detail: < 50% ST resolution, ongoing pain or instability: rescue PCI. Otherwise angiography 2-24 h after lysis.

steps.title: Risk-stratify
steps.detail: Very high risk (shock, refractory pain, life-threatening arrhythmia, mechanical complication, acute HF, recurrent dynamic ST changes): angiography < 2 h. High risk (confirmed NSTEMI, dynamic ST/T changes, GRACE > 140): < 24 h.

steps.title: Antithrombotics
steps.detail: Aspirin + P2Y12 inhibitor (ticagrelor or prasugrel at PCI; clopidogrel with lysis or oral anticoagulant) + parenteral anticoagulant.

steps.title: Secondary prevention
steps.detail: High-intensity statin, ACE-i/ARB, beta-blocker if LVEF ≤ 40%, MRA/SGLT2i if HFrEF, cardiac rehabilitation.

Inferior STEMI: record V4R; avoid nitrates if RV infarct.
Tearing chest/back pain, pulse deficit or wide mediastinum: exclude aortic dissection before lysis or anticoagulation.

Prasugrel after previous stroke or TIA.

pearls.text: Posterior MI: ST depression with tall R waves in V1-V3; record V7-V9.

consultantNotes.evidence:
- **ESC ACS 2023:** primary PCI if feasible within 120 min; otherwise fibrinolysis within 10 min; half-dose tenecteplase ≥ 75 y; pharmaco-invasive angiography 2-24 h; NSTE-ACS timing by risk.
- **ACC/AHA 2025:** similar framework for reperfusion, P2Y12 choice and early invasive strategy in high-risk NSTE-ACS.
consultantNotes.controversies: - Routine beta-blockers after MI with preserved EF (REDUCE-AMI: no benefit).
consultantNotes.indiaNotes:
- Many Indian STEMI patients are young, diabetic and present late; the pharmaco-invasive (lysis then transfer) model is realistic in most districts.
- Streptokinase remains in use for cost reasons; it is less effective and causes hypotension.

quiz.explanation: If PCI cannot happen within 120 min, lyse.

topics.title: Acute heart failure and pulmonary oedema
topics.summary: Profile the patient as warm/cold and wet/dry. Warm-wet: IV loop diuretic plus vasodilator if SBP > 110 and CPAP/NIV for pulmonary oedema. Cold: cardiogenic shock pathway. Always find the trigger.

steps.title: Stabilise
steps.detail: Sit up, O2 to SpO2 > 90%, CPAP/NIV if RR > 25 or SpO2 < 90%. ECG, troponin, NT-proBNP, echo.

steps.title: Profile
steps.detail: Warm-wet (commonest), cold-wet, cold-dry, warm-dry.

steps.title: Find the trigger
steps.detail: ACS, hypertensive emergency, arrhythmia, mechanical cause (valve rupture, VSR), PE, infection, tamponade, non-adherence, NSAIDs, renal failure, anaemia, thyroid.

steps.title: Loop diuretic
steps.detail: Furosemide 20-40 mg IV if naïve, or 1-2 × the oral daily dose. Spot urine Na < 50-70 mmol/L at 2 h or urine < 100-150 mL/h at 6 h: double the dose; then add a thiazide or acetazolamide.

steps.title: Vasodilator
steps.detail: GTN 10-20 mcg/min IV, titrate to 200 mcg/min.

steps.title: Shock
steps.detail: Cardiogenic shock pathway (module 3); no vasodilators.

steps.title: Guideline therapy
steps.detail: ACE-i/ARNI, beta-blocker, MRA, SGLT2i with rapid up-titration.

doseCards.dose: 20-40 mg (naïve) or 1-2 × daily oral dose
10-20 mcg/min, up to 200 mcg/min

redFlags.text: SBP < 90 with cold peripheries: cardiogenic shock.
New murmur after MI: papillary muscle rupture or VSR.

pitfalls.text: Nitrates in severe aortic stenosis or RV infarct.

pearls.text: Hypertensive 'flash' pulmonary oedema responds dramatically to high-dose nitrates with NIV.

nodes.text: Sit up, O2, CPAP/NIV if distressed; ECG, echo, BNP
Double loop dose; add thiazide or acetazolamide

consultantNotes.evidence:
- **ESC HF 2021:** NIV for respiratory distress; loop diuretics with early natriuresis check; vasodilators if SBP > 110; routine opioids not recommended.
- **ESC HF 2023 update:** rapid initiation and up-titration of guideline therapy before and soon after discharge.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes:
- Rheumatic mitral stenosis with AF is still a common cause of pulmonary oedema in India: control rate and diurese; consider balloon valvotomy.
- Peripartum cardiomyopathy: see module 30.

topics.title: AF with rapid ventricular response in the ICU
topics.summary: Unstable: synchronised cardioversion (≥ 200 J biphasic). Stable: treat triggers (sepsis, hypovolaemia, K+, Mg2+, catecholamines), then rate control with a beta-blocker or diltiazem if LVEF > 40%, or amiodarone/digoxin if LVEF ≤ 40% or hypotensive. Assess anticoagulation.

steps.title: Unstable?
steps.detail: Shock, ischaemia, acute HF or syncope caused by the arrhythmia: synchronised DC cardioversion, initial ≥ 200 J biphasic, under sedation.

steps.title: Triggers
steps.detail: Sepsis, hypovolaemia, hypoxia, pain, K+ < 4 or Mg2+ low, high-dose catecholamines, thyrotoxicosis, PE, alcohol withdrawal, pericarditis. Correct K+ to 4-4.5 and give Mg 2 g IV.

steps.title: LVEF > 40%
steps.detail: Metoprolol 2.5-5 mg IV (repeat to 15 mg) or esmolol infusion, or diltiazem 0.25 mg/kg IV.

steps.title: LVEF ≤ 40% or hypotension
steps.detail: Amiodarone 300 mg IV over 1 h then 900 mg/24 h, or digoxin 0.5 mg IV then 0.25 mg 6-hourly (max 1-1.5 mg).

steps.title: Lenient
steps.detail: Initial heart rate target < 110/min; tighter only if symptoms persist.

steps.title: Elective cardioversion
steps.detail: If AF > 24 h and not anticoagulated: TOE to exclude LA thrombus or ≥ 3 weeks anticoagulation first.

steps.title: Stroke risk
steps.detail: CHA2DS2-VA ≥ 2: anticoagulate unless bleeding risk prohibitive; reassess new-onset sepsis-related AF after recovery.

redFlags.text: Irregular wide-complex tachycardia at > 250/min (pre-excited AF): no AV-nodal blockers; cardiovert.
AF with hypotension in sepsis: is it the cause or the consequence? Treat sepsis first unless rate > 150 and clearly causal.

pitfalls.text: Diltiazem or beta-blocker boluses in decompensated HFrEF.
Cardioverting long-standing AF without anticoagulation or TOE.

pearls.text: New-onset AF in septic shock often reverts as shock resolves; reducing catecholamines and correcting Mg/K helps.

nodes.text: Synchronised cardioversion ≥ 200 J; amiodarone if recurs
Correct triggers: fluids, K+, Mg2+, sepsis, pain, catecholamines

consultantNotes.evidence:
- **ESC AF 2024 (AF-CARE):** beta-blockers, diltiazem/verapamil (LVEF > 40%) or digoxin for rate control; amiodarone for acute rate control in haemodynamic instability or severely reduced EF; lenient initial target < 110/min; CHA2DS2-VA for stroke risk; TOE or 3 weeks anticoagulation before cardioversion if AF > 24 h.
- **AHA 2025:** ≥ 200 J initial energy for AF cardioversion.
consultantNotes.controversies: - Anticoagulation for AF that occurs only during critical illness.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes: - Rheumatic mitral stenosis is a common cause of AF in India; it is a 'valvular' AF where warfarin (not DOACs) is indicated.

verify.reason: ESC 2024 uses a 24 h threshold for early cardioversion without prior anticoagulation; older guidance used 48 h. Confirm local policy.

topics.title: Ventricular tachycardia, wide-complex tachycardia and electrical storm
topics.summary: Treat a regular wide-complex tachycardia as VT until proven otherwise. Unstable: synchronised cardioversion. Stable: cardioversion under sedation or IV amiodarone. Torsades: magnesium and remove QT drugs. Electrical storm: sedate, beta-block, amiodarone, correct electrolytes, treat ischaemia.

steps.title: Pulse?
steps.detail: Pulseless: ALS shockable pathway (module 2). Pulse present: assess stability.

steps.title: Synchronised cardioversion
steps.detail: 120-200 J biphasic, escalate; sedate if conscious. Polymorphic VT: unsynchronised shock.

steps.title: Cardioversion or drug
steps.detail: ESC 2022 favours synchronised cardioversion if anaesthesia risk is low; otherwise amiodarone 300 mg IV over 10-60 min (procainamide where available). Adenosine only for regular monomorphic WCT when SVT with aberrancy is likely.

steps.title: QT-related
steps.detail: Magnesium 2 g IV; stop QT-prolonging drugs; K+ to 4.5-5; if bradycardia-dependent, isoprenaline or overdrive pacing.

steps.title: ≥ 3 sustained VT/VF in 24 h
steps.detail: Deep sedation (± intubation), beta-blockade (propranolol or esmolol), amiodarone, correct K+/Mg2+, urgent angiography if ischaemia; ICD reprogramming; ablation or MCS in refractory cases.

steps.title: Find the cause
steps.detail: Ischaemia, scar, cardiomyopathy, myocarditis, electrolytes, drugs (QT), channelopathy. Cardiology referral for ICD/ablation.

doseCards.dose: 300 mg over 10-60 min, then 900 mg/24 h
2 g over 10-15 min; repeat or infuse 3-10 mg/min if recurs

pitfalls.text: Assuming haemodynamic stability means SVT; VT can be well tolerated.

pearls.text: Incessant VT with fever and new heart failure in a young Indian patient: consider myocarditis, including scrub typhus, dengue or diphtheria.

Correct electrolytes, look for ischaemia, cardiology review

consultantNotes.evidence:
- **ESC VA 2022:** synchronised cardioversion first line for tolerated sustained monomorphic VT when anaesthetic risk is low; procainamide or amiodarone otherwise; management of electrical storm and torsades.
- **AHA 2025:** unsynchronised shocks for polymorphic VT; avoid calcium-channel blockers in WCT.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes:
- Procainamide is not available in India; amiodarone and lidocaine are the IV options.
- Organophosphate and aluminium phosphide poisoning cause QT prolongation and ventricular arrhythmias (module 28).

quiz.explanation: Verapamil/diltiazem can cause collapse in VT.

topics.title: Bradycardia, heart block and temporary pacing
topics.summary: Look for adverse features and reversible causes (drugs, K+, ischaemia, hypothermia, hypothyroidism, raised ICP). Atropine first; if it fails or the block is infranodal, adrenaline or isoprenaline infusion and transcutaneous then transvenous pacing.

steps.title: Assess
steps.detail: Shock, syncope, ischaemia, heart failure, pauses > 3 s, Mobitz II, complete heart block with wide QRS, ventricular standstill.

steps.title: Atropine
steps.detail: 0.5-1 mg IV every 3-5 min to 3 mg (ineffective after heart transplant and in infranodal block).

steps.title: Chronotropes
steps.detail: Adrenaline 2-10 mcg/min or isoprenaline 1-10 mcg/min (dopamine 5-20 mcg/kg/min alternative).

steps.title: Transcutaneous
steps.detail: Rate 60-70, increase output until capture; confirm with femoral pulse; analgesia/sedation. Bridge to transvenous.

steps.title: Transvenous
steps.detail: Right internal jugular or left subclavian with ultrasound; ventricular capture threshold < 1 mA, output 3 × threshold.

steps.title: Treat
steps.detail: Beta-blocker (glucagon), calcium-channel blocker (calcium, high-dose insulin), digoxin (Fab fragments), hyperkalaemia (calcium), inferior MI (often resolves after reperfusion), hypothermia, hypothyroidism, raised ICP, Lyme or infiltrative disease.

doseCards.dose: 0.5-1 mg every 3-5 min (max 3 mg)
1-10 mcg/min

redFlags.text: Complete heart block with broad escape or pauses: pace early.
Bradycardia with hypertension and irregular breathing: Cushing response (raised ICP).

pitfalls.text: Assuming electrical capture means mechanical capture.

pearls.text: Yellow oleander (Thevetia) poisoning in South India causes digoxin-like bradyarrhythmias; anti-digoxin Fab is effective but rarely available (module 28).

nodes.text: Adrenaline or isoprenaline infusion; transcutaneous pacing

consultantNotes.evidence:
- **ESC pacing 2021:** acute management of bradycardia with atropine, isoprenaline/adrenaline, and temporary pacing only when needed (transvenous pacing has complications).
- **AHA 2025:** atropine 1 mg; adrenaline infusion or pacing if refractory.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes: - Temporary pacing leads and pacing boxes may be held only by cardiology; know where they are at night.

topics.title: Hypertensive emergencies
topics.summary: Hypertensive emergency means severe BP elevation with acute organ damage. Lower BP with titratable IV drugs to a target and timeline set by the organ involved; avoid precipitous falls except in aortic dissection, pulmonary oedema and eclampsia.

steps.title: Confirm organ damage
steps.detail: Encephalopathy, stroke/ICH, ACS, pulmonary oedema, aortic dissection, AKI, TMA, retinopathy (malignant), eclampsia. No organ damage = urgency: oral therapy, not IV.

steps.title: Pick target by organ
steps.detail: See table. General: MAP fall ≤ 20-25% in the first hours.

steps.title: Pick drug
steps.detail: Labetalol (most), nicardipine (stroke, encephalopathy, AKI), GTN (ACS, pulmonary oedema), esmolol + vasodilator (dissection), labetalol or nicardipine plus magnesium (eclampsia).

steps.title: Arterial line
steps.detail: BP every 5-15 min during titration; neurological checks.

steps.title: Find cause
steps.detail: Non-adherence, renal artery stenosis, phaeochromocytoma, drugs (cocaine, amphetamine, MAOI), pre-eclampsia, renal disease.

Severe hypertension with tachycardia, sweating, headache: phaeochromocytoma or sympathomimetic toxicity (no beta-blocker first).

pitfalls.text: Treating asymptomatic severe hypertension with IV drugs.

pearls.text: In stroke and ICH, see module 20 for current targets (INTERACT trials).

nodes.text: Urgency: oral therapy, review in 24-48 h
Dissection: esmolol then vasodilator; SBP < 120, HR < 60 now

consultantNotes.evidence:
- **ESC Council on Hypertension 2019:** presentation-specific targets and preferred drugs for hypertensive emergencies.
- **ESC 2024 hypertension guideline:** reaffirms the approach and the distinction from hypertensive urgency.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes:
- Uncontrolled hypertension is common and under-treated in India; malignant hypertension with AKI is a frequent ICU admission in young adults.
- IV nicardipine is often unavailable; labetalol, GTN and nitroprusside are the mainstays.

quiz.stem: Hypertensive urgency without organ damage is treated with:
Before thrombolysis for stroke, BP must be below:

drugs.name: Aspirin
drugs.indications: All ACS unless contraindicated.
drugs.adultDose: Loading 150-300 mg orally (chewed, non-enteric coated) or 75-250 mg IV; then 75-100 mg daily.
drugs.preparationIndia: 75 mg, 150 mg and 325 mg tablets; chewable formulations widely available.
drugs.cautions: Active bleeding, true allergy.

drugs.name: Ticagrelor
drugs.indications: ACS (with aspirin), PCI.
drugs.adultDose: 180 mg loading, then 90 mg twice daily for 12 months (default).
drugs.preparationIndia: 90 mg tablets (can be crushed for NG tube).
drugs.cautions: Dyspnoea, bradyarrhythmia, bleeding; not with fibrinolysis (use clopidogrel).

drugs.name: Clopidogrel
drugs.indications: With fibrinolysis; when ticagrelor/prasugrel unavailable or contraindicated; patients on oral anticoagulants.
drugs.adultDose: PCI: 600 mg loading then 75 mg daily. With fibrinolysis: 300 mg loading (75 mg if age > 75 years), then 75 mg daily.
drugs.preparationIndia: 75 mg and 300 mg tablets; inexpensive.
drugs.cautions: Variable response (CYP2C19 polymorphism, common in South Asians).

drugs.name: Unfractionated heparin (UFH)
drugs.indications: Primary PCI; adjunct to fibrinolysis; NSTE-ACS when early invasive strategy; AF or LV thrombus when rapid reversal may be needed.
drugs.adultDose: Primary PCI: 70-100 U/kg IV bolus. With fibrinolysis: 60 U/kg bolus (max 4000 U), then 12 U/kg/h (max 1000 U/h), aPTT 1.5-2.0 × control (≈ 50-70 s) for 24-48 h.
drugs.preparationIndia: 5000 U/mL (5 mL vials = 25 000 U). Infusion 25 000 U in 50 mL = 500 U/mL.
drugs.cautions: Heparin-induced thrombocytopenia; bleeding; monitor platelets.
drugs.monitoring: aPTT (or anti-Xa) 6 h after start and each change; platelets on alternate days.

drugs.name: Enoxaparin
drugs.indications: NSTE-ACS; adjunct to fibrinolysis; VTE treatment.
drugs.adultDose: NSTE-ACS: 1 mg/kg SC every 12 h. With fibrinolysis: age < 75: 30 mg IV bolus + 1 mg/kg SC 15 min later then every 12 h (first 2 doses max 100 mg); age ≥ 75: no bolus, 0.75 mg/kg SC every 12 h (first 2 doses max 75 mg). CrCl < 30: 1 mg/kg once daily.
drugs.preparationIndia: Prefilled syringes 40, 60, 80 mg; biosimilars available.
drugs.cautions: Accumulates in renal failure; partial protamine reversal only.

drugs.name: Tenecteplase
drugs.indications: STEMI within 12 h when primary PCI cannot be done within 120 min of diagnosis.
drugs.adultDose: Single IV bolus by weight: < 60 kg 30 mg; 60-69 kg 35 mg; 70-79 kg 40 mg; 80-89 kg 45 mg; ≥ 90 kg 50 mg. Half dose in patients ≥ 75 years.
drugs.preparationIndia: 40 mg vials (8000 U) reconstituted to 5 mg/mL; Indian biosimilars available (20, 30, 40 mg).
drugs.cautions: Absolute contraindications: previous ICH or unknown-origin stroke, ischaemic stroke within 6 months, CNS tumour/AV malformation, major trauma/surgery/head injury within 1 month, GI bleed within 1 month, bleeding disorder, aortic dissection, non-compressible punctures within 24 h.
drugs.verify: Check the biosimilar product's own dose table.

drugs.name: Streptokinase
drugs.indications: STEMI fibrinolysis where tenecteplase/alteplase are unavailable or unaffordable.
drugs.adultDose: 1.5 million units IV over 30-60 min.
drugs.preparationIndia: 1.5 MU vials; reconstitute in 100 mL NS.
drugs.cautions: Hypotension during infusion (slow or pause), allergic reactions; antibodies form, do not repeat after 5 days. Less effective than fibrin-specific agents.

drugs.name: Glyceryl trinitrate (nitroglycerin)
drugs.indications: Acute pulmonary oedema with SBP > 110 mmHg; ongoing ischaemic pain; hypertensive emergency with ACS or pulmonary oedema.
drugs.adultDose: Sublingual 0.4-0.5 mg; IV 10-20 mcg/min, increase by 5-10 mcg/min every 3-5 min, up to 200 mcg/min.
drugs.preparationIndia: 5 mg/mL ampoules (25 mg/5 mL). 50 mg in 50 mL NS/D5 = 1 mg/mL (1000 mcg/mL). Use non-PVC tubing if possible.
drugs.cautions: Avoid with SBP < 90, RV infarction, severe aortic stenosis, PDE-5 inhibitor within 24-48 h. Headache; tachyphylaxis.

drugs.name: Furosemide
drugs.indications: Congestion in acute heart failure.
drugs.adultDose: Diuretic-naïve: 20-40 mg IV. On oral loop diuretic: IV dose 1-2 × the daily oral dose. Check spot urine sodium after 2 h (target > 50-70 mmol/L) or urine output > 100-150 mL/h over 6 h; if inadequate, double the dose (max ~400-600 mg/day).
drugs.preparationIndia: 10 mg/mL, 2 mL ampoules; infusion 250 mg in 50 mL.
drugs.cautions: Hypokalaemia, hypomagnesaemia, ototoxicity with rapid high doses (≤ 4 mg/min).

drugs.name: Amiodarone
drugs.indications: AF rate or rhythm control in critically ill or reduced EF; haemodynamically tolerated VT; electrical storm.
drugs.adultDose: 300 mg (or 5-7 mg/kg) IV over 20-60 min, then 900 mg over 24 h; total ≤ 2.2 g/24 h.
drugs.preparationIndia: 150 mg/3 mL ampoules; dilute in 5% dextrose; central line preferred for infusion.
drugs.cautions: Hypotension, bradycardia, phlebitis, QT prolongation; thyroid, liver and lung toxicity with prolonged use; interacts with warfarin and digoxin.

drugs.name: Diltiazem
drugs.indications: AF/flutter rate control when LVEF > 40%.
drugs.adultDose: 0.25 mg/kg IV over 2 min (≈ 15-20 mg), repeat 0.35 mg/kg after 15 min if needed; infusion 5-15 mg/h.
drugs.preparationIndia: 25 mg/5 mL injection (availability variable).
drugs.cautions: Avoid in HFrEF, hypotension, pre-excited AF, wide-complex tachycardia.

drugs.name: Metoprolol
drugs.indications: AF rate control; ACS (tachycardia, hypertension, no heart failure).
drugs.adultDose: IV 2.5-5 mg over 2 min, repeat every 5 min to max 15 mg. Oral 25-100 mg twice daily.
drugs.preparationIndia: 5 mg/5 mL injection; tablets 25, 50 mg.
drugs.cautions: Avoid in acute HF, shock, bradycardia, severe bronchospasm, cocaine-related ACS.

drugs.name: Esmolol
drugs.indications: Rate control in AF when titratable control is needed; aortic dissection (with vasodilator); hypertensive emergencies with tachycardia.
drugs.adultDose: 500 mcg/kg over 1 min, then 50-300 mcg/kg/min.
drugs.preparationIndia: 100 mg/10 mL vials (10 mg/mL); 2.5 g/250 mL premixed bags in some hospitals.
drugs.cautions: Hypotension; bradycardia.

drugs.name: Digoxin
drugs.indications: AF rate control, especially with reduced EF or hypotension, as add-on.
drugs.adultDose: IV loading 0.5 mg, then 0.25 mg every 6 h to total 1-1.5 mg (reduce in renal failure and elderly). Maintenance 0.0625-0.25 mg daily by renal function.
drugs.preparationIndia: 0.25 mg/mL injection (2 mL = 0.5 mg); 0.25 mg tablets.
drugs.renalHepatic: Renally cleared: reduce dose; target level 0.5-0.9 ng/mL.
drugs.cautions: Toxicity with hypokalaemia, hypomagnesaemia, hypercalcaemia, amiodarone; avoid in pre-excitation.

drugs.name: Adenosine
drugs.indications: Regular narrow-complex tachycardia (SVT); diagnostic in stable regular monomorphic wide-complex tachycardia.
drugs.adultDose: 6 mg rapid IV push with 20 mL flush; then 12 mg (repeat 12 mg once per ESC/AHA practice). 3 mg if central line, heart transplant, or on dipyridamole.
drugs.preparationIndia: 3 mg/mL (2 mL = 6 mg) vials.
drugs.cautions: Asthma (bronchospasm), pre-excited AF, irregular or polymorphic WCT; transient asystole is expected.

drugs.name: Atropine
drugs.indications: Symptomatic bradycardia.
drugs.adultDose: 0.5-1 mg IV every 3-5 min to max 3 mg.
drugs.preparationIndia: 0.6 mg/mL ampoules.
drugs.cautions: Ineffective in heart transplant and infranodal block (Mobitz II, wide-escape CHB).

drugs.name: Isoprenaline (isoproterenol)
drugs.indications: Bradycardia bridge to pacing; bradycardia-dependent torsades.
drugs.adultDose: Infusion 1-10 mcg/min (start 2-5 mcg/min).
drugs.preparationIndia: Availability limited; 2 mg/mL or 0.2 mg/mL ampoules depending on supplier.
drugs.cautions: Tachyarrhythmia, hypotension (beta-2 vasodilation), myocardial ischaemia.

drugs.name: Magnesium sulfate
drugs.indications: Torsades de pointes; adjunct in AF and VT when Mg low.
drugs.adultDose: 2 g IV over 10-15 min; may repeat; aim Mg > 1 mmol/L.
drugs.preparationIndia: 50% (500 mg/mL) 2 mL ampoules.
drugs.cautions: Hypotension, loss of reflexes at high levels; caution in renal failure.

drugs.name: Labetalol
drugs.indications: Hypertensive emergencies (encephalopathy, stroke, pre-eclampsia, aortic dissection with tachycardia control).
drugs.adultDose: 0.25-0.5 mg/kg IV bolus (typically 20 mg) over 2 min, repeat 20-80 mg every 10 min (max 300 mg); or infusion 1-2 mg/min (some protocols up to 4 mg/min) until target, then reduce.
drugs.preparationIndia: 5 mg/mL, 4 mL ampoules (20 mg). Infusion: undiluted 5 mg/mL or 100 mg in 100 mL.
drugs.cautions: Bradycardia, heart block, acute HF, asthma.

drugs.name: Nicardipine
drugs.indications: Hypertensive emergencies (stroke, encephalopathy, AKI).
drugs.adultDose: 5 mg/h IV, increase by 2.5 mg/h every 5-15 min to max 15 mg/h.
drugs.preparationIndia: Limited availability; check local supply.
drugs.cautions: Reflex tachycardia; avoid in severe aortic stenosis and acute HF.

drugs.name: Sodium nitroprusside
drugs.indications: Hypertensive emergencies with acute LV failure or aortic dissection (with beta-blocker) when other agents fail.
drugs.adultDose: 0.3-10 mcg/kg/min; use the lowest dose and shortest duration (< 48-72 h).
drugs.preparationIndia: 50 mg vials; 50 mg in 50 mL D5 = 1000 mcg/mL; protect from light.
drugs.cautions: Cyanide and thiocyanate toxicity (renal/hepatic failure, high doses); rebound; raises ICP.

verify.reason: Tenecteplase (including Indian biosimilars), reteplase, alteplase and streptokinase are all used in India; streptokinase remains common in public hospitals because of cost. Confirm the agent and dosing used locally.
IV nicardipine has limited availability in India; clevidipine is generally unavailable. Labetalol, GTN, esmolol and sodium nitroprusside are the usual IV agents.
